what_its_for: Hydroquinone is a skin-lightening cream or gel used to fade dark spots, uneven skin tone, freckles, and discoloration caused by sun damage, aging, pregnancy (melasma), or certain medications. It works by slowing down the skin's production of melanin, which is the pigment that gives skin its color.
how_to_take: Hydroquinone is applied directly to your skin — NOT taken by mouth. Wash and dry your hands and the affected skin area before applying. Use a small amount and gently rub it into only the darkened skin areas. Try to avoid getting it on normal, healthy skin around the spots. Wash your hands thoroughly after applying. Always apply a broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) during the day when using this product, as sun exposure can make dark spots worse.
dosing: Apply hydroquinone to the affected skin areas twice daily — once in the morning and once at night — or as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. Use only a thin layer. Do not apply more than directed, as using too much will not make it work faster and may cause more side effects. Most courses of treatment last no longer than 3 to 6 months without a break. Do not use it for longer than your doctor recommends.
missed_dose: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled application, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular routine. Do not double up or apply extra to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store hydroquinone at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from direct sunlight, heat, and moisture. Do not freeze. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep this product out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it if it turns dark brown or gray in color — this may mean the product has oxidized and is no longer effective.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting hydroquinone in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on broken or irritated skin. If it gets into your eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water. Avoid sun exposure as much as possible while using this medication — always wear sunscreen, protective clothing, and a hat when outdoors. Do not use tanning beds or sunlamps. Avoid using other skin products on the same area at the same time unless your doctor says it is okay, especially products containing peroxides (like benzoyl peroxide) or harsh exfoliants, as these may cause skin irritation or make the cream turn a dark color on your skin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience: a skin rash, severe redness, blistering, burning, or itching that does not go away; unusual darkening or bluish-gray discoloration of the skin (this could be a rare condition called ochronosis); signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; no improvement in your skin after 2 months of use; or if your skin condition gets worse.
when_it_works: Hydroquinone does not work overnight. You may start to notice some lightening of dark spots after about 4 to 6 weeks of regular use. It usually takes 2 to 3 months of consistent use to see the full benefit. Be patient and keep using it as directed. If you do not see any improvement after 2 months, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Hydroquinone is generally not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: This product should generally not be used in children under 12 years old unless specifically directed by a doctor. Older adults: Use with caution; older skin may be more sensitive. People with sensitive skin or eczema: Use with caution and talk to your doctor first, as hydroquinone may cause more irritation on sensitive or already inflamed skin.
